newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 28.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
GUJRAL SAYS KASHMIR TALK OFFER ONLY TO MISGUIDED YOUTHS

Prime Minister Gujral indicated on Sunday he was unwilling to open a dialogue with the All Party Hurriyat Conference saying he did not want to negotiate the secular unity and integrity of the country. "My offer of talk is for all those who have been misled by false propaganda -- particularly the youth. But this does not mean that I am willing to negotiate the status of Jammu and Kashmir which is and will continue to be an integral part of India," he said. Gujral said the rehabilitation of the estranged youths in Kashmir was an integral part of countering the proxy war in Jammu and Kashmir.
The Economic Times
INDIA BRIEFS U.S. ON STAND ON QUANTITATIVE RESTRICTIONS

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram met U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright in Kuala Lumpur and briefed her on India's stand on removal of quantitative restrictions on imports. Chidambaram later said Albright had promised to convey India's concerns to U.S. officials. The United States was putting pressure on India at the World Trade Organisation for a faster phase out of all quantitative restrictions on imports into India. The developed nations have moved the dispute settlement mechanism of the WTO to settle the issue. India still has about 60 days left to settle the issue before it goes to the dispute settlement mechanism.
INCENTIVES FOR POWER SECTOR PLANNED

The government will soon announce a package of incentives for the power sector which will enable easier financing of upcoming projects. It will include relaxation on guarantee norms of financial institutions, introduction of subsidised interest rates for renovation and modernisation of projects and, amendments of procedures in the calculation of depreciation. The private companies which source their debt requirements from the Indian financial institutions are likely to be exempted from the mandatory requirement of providing 100 percent guarantees for borrowings. The Minister of State of Power said a higher depreciation, a five year tax holiday and a flexible credit facility would help private power projects.
GOVERNMENT FIRM TAPS EURO AT 135 POINTS ABOVE U.S. TREASURY

The 12 year, $100 million Euro note issue launched by the Power Finance Corporation (PFC) last Friday is rated 135 basis points above the U.S. Treasury. The instrument was floated to finance projects in the power sector. At 135 basis points above U.S. Treasury, the interest rate for the loan will be about 7.5 percent. This is despite Moody's bearishness about investments in India when the PFC came up with its proposal for the loan. The loan was taken on a bullet repayment basis. It was the first external commercial borrowing by the company in fiscal 1997/98 (April-March).
Financial Express
BULLS SURGE AHEAD

The Bombay bourse sensitive index gained 64 points to close at 4,189.81 points against the previous week's close of 4,125.81 points on July 18. The last day of the current settlement saw hectic activitY in select non-specified stocks. Among the scrips that recorded a 52-week high are those of Aptech (487 rupees), Essel Packaging (173.50 rupees), ICI India (237 rupees), India Shaving (625 rupees) and Kodak India (575 rupees).
TWO JAPANESE FIRMS TO PICK UP STAKE IN INDIAN COMPANY

Japanese majors Itochu Corp and Mitsui Petrochemicals Corp will pick up 35 percent and five percent stakes respectively in Indo Rama Synthetics Ltd's 12 billion rupee purified terephthalic acid project. Indo Rama holds a 60 percent stake in the venture. The capacity of this proposed plant is 350,000 tonnes a year. The three companies will sign the agreement on August 4. Mitsui will be allowed to increase its stake to 25 percent over a period. The project has a debt-equity ratio of 2:1. It is expected to go on stream by the year 1999. The overseas companies will bring in the latest technology.
UK COMPANY TO DILUTE STAKE IN RATNA OILFIELD

The Essar group and Premier Oil Plc of Britain, who are the main partners in the Ratna oilfield development project are holding talks on dilution of Premier's stake. Essar holds a 50 percent share in the venture, state-owned Oil and Natural Gas Commission 40 percent and Premier Oil 10 percent. Industry sources said Essar had held talks with the U.S. major Atlantic Richfield Co and Italian energy group Eni and Premier Oil might give up its entire stake and move out of the project.
Business Standard
INFLATION DIPS TO 4.43 PCT

The annual rate of inflation fell by another 0.27 percentage points to touch a one-year low of 4.43 percent for the week ended July 12. It was 5.88 percent in the corresponding week last year. The wholesale price index (base 1981/82=100) for all commodities rose 0.1 percent to reach 325.2 (provisional) during the week compared to 325 (provisional) a week earlier.
EXTERNAL DEBT FLAT AT $92 BLN

India's external debt declined to $92 billion at the end of March 1997 from $92.20 billion at the end of March 1996. The debt to service ratio fell to 20 percent in 1996/97 (April-March) from 25.7 percent in 1995/96 while the debt to gross domestic product ratio dropped to 25.2 percent in 1996/97 from 28.7 percent in 1995/96. Although India's external debt was growing at an annual average rate of 3.3 percent since 1990/91, the growth rate in rupee terms was around 15.9 percent because of the depreciation of the rupee.
MONEY MARKET REGULATOR ON CARDS

Banks and primary dealers are forming an autonomous, self-regulatory body for money and securities market trading. It will promote a liquid debt and derivatives market and set common standards for the participants. It will be modelled after the Zurich-based International Securities Association and the International Securities Managements Association. Named as the Fixed Income Money Market and Derivatives Association, it will help the interbank term rate to take off. This will help the money and gilt market which had no authority so far to take up its cause or put in place a regulatory framework. The daily turnover of this segment is about 100 billion rupees.
The Observer
BOMBAY BOURSE TO EXPORT ITS TRADE-RELATED SOFTWARE

The Bombay bourse (BSE) will sell its stock market related software system overseas. The BSE has appointed CMC and Tandem as its marketing agents. Bangladesh has already placed an order with the CMC through the Chittagong Stock Exchange for the software. This means the carry forward trading system (locally known as the Badla system) will go overseas. The Badla system is purely an Indian one. It is not known outside the country now. The software package of the BSE includes the entire trading system and Badla is a part of it. The version bought by the Chittagong Stock Exchange is a smaller one of the online trading system.
